questions.question: What does the emergency air line supply air to?
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up.
It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
It makes turning a vehicle easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops wheels from locking up when braking hard. If ABS detects the wheels are about to lock, it reduces brake pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: Before driving, how do you make sure air reaches all trailers?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for escaping air.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that air reaches all trailers. Let air pressure build up, then send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is reaching the whole vehicle.

questions.question: What is true about combination vehicles?

options.text: They often have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
They are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
They require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Driving combination vehicles requires more skill than driving single commercial vehicles. Combination vehicles are longer, heavier, and roll over more easily.

questions.question: How can a driver help prevent a rollover?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too quickly. To prevent rollovers, keep the vehicle's center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: What happens when an air supply control is in the "emergency" position?

options.text: It turns on the air supply.
It applies the trailer emergency brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It applies the trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. When an air supply control is in the "emergency" position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn or change lanes too quickly.

questions.question: What is off-tracking?

options.text: When a vehicle's front wheels follow a different path than its rear wheels.
When a vehicle's wheels all follow the exact same path.
When a load shifts during a turn.
When a vehicle's wheels run over a curb during a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a vehicle's front wheels follow a different path than its rear wheels.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking.

questions.question: What happens when combination vehicles are lightly loaded?

options.text: They should be loaded with most weight in the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: When a combination vehicle is lightly loaded, it may have poor traction. Wheels can lock up easily when stopping a lightly-loaded vehicle.

questions.question: When a vehicle goes around a corner, what do the rear wheels do?

options.text: They follow the same path as the front wheels.
They follow a different path than the front wheels.
They should not be a concern to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: They follow a different path than the front wheels.
questions.explanation: When any vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. Longer vehicles have more off-tracking than shorter vehicles.

questions.question: During a trip, the ____ should be open.
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, open all shut-off valves except the ones at the back of the trailer. This keeps air flowing to the brakes on all trailers and prevents air from escaping from the back.

questions.question: Compared to other commercial vehicles, combination vehicles need more road space because they are longer and they:

options.text: Need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles because they are longer and need extra space to turn and stop. Managing space properly is very important when driving a combination vehicle.

questions.question: If you do not keep the fifth wheel plate properly greased, it could:
questions.explanation: If the fifth wheel plate is not properly greased, friction builds up between the tractor and trailer. This can cause steering problems.

questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake and connects to the ____ valves.
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Only when the trailer is carrying a load
Only to test the trailer brakes
Only in bad weather when the trailer might skid

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve is used to test the trailer brakes. Never use it while driving because it can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: If you are not sure if a trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: If air lines are color-coded, which color is used for emergency lines?
questions.explanation: Color-coded air lines use blue for service lines and red for emergency lines.

questions.question: If color-coded, which color identifies emergency or supply lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded to help drivers connect them correctly. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: You should not use the trailer hand valve while driving because:

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it while the vehicle is moving can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle goes around a corner:

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes.
The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
It is best to let the rear wheels drive over the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
questions.explanation: When turning a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking and is especially noticeable on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that helps the battery recharge.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: On combination vehicles with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system. It works if the trailer leaks or breaks away.

questions.question: How can you best tell that your trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: By looking at other drivers' faces.
By seeing it in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: By seeing it in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The best way to notice a trailer skid early is to see the trailer move off-course in your mirrors.

questions.question: When will an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
When you are experiencing a trailer jackknife.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: An automatic tractor protection valve pops out if air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: What can be difficult to drive over with a trailer that has low clearance underneath?
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be difficult to cross with a trailer that has low clearance. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers are especially challenging.

questions.question: Before you back your tractor under the trailer, your trailer brakes should be:
questions.explanation: When coupling a tractor and trailer, you must make sure your trailer brakes are locked before backing under the trailer.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high when coupling?

options.text: It will not make a difference when coupling.

questions.explanation: Before coupling, the trailer must be at the right height. If too low, the nose may be damaged. If too high, the trailer may not couple correctly.

questions.question: What color are emergency air lines usually coded?
questions.explanation: The service air line is coded blue. The emergency air line is coded red.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, which way should you back?
questions.explanation: If you cannot back in a straight line, back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: When is a trailer most likely to swing out?

options.text: When traveling in a straight line.

questions.explanation: An empty trailer needs a longer stopping distance than a loaded one. An empty or lightly loaded trailer is most likely to swing out and hit other vehicles.
